cases.title: Browser says there is no internet connection
patterns: you are not connected to the internet
cases.meaning: The browser could not reach the internet at all. The problem is usually between the computer and the router, not the website.
causes: Wi-Fi is off or connected to the wrong network
The router or modem has lost its connection
A network adapter or driver problem

cases.title: Website address could not be found (DNS error)
patterns: server dns address could not be found
cases.meaning: The computer is on a network but could not turn a website name into an address. Other devices on the same network may or may not have the same problem.
causes: The DNS server given by the router is not answering
A stale DNS cache on the computer
The internet connection behind the router is down

cases.title: Connection timed out
cases.meaning: The browser reached out but got no reply in time. It can be the website, but a weak or unstable connection is also common.
causes: A weak or unstable Wi-Fi signal
A slow or interrupted internet service
A proxy, VPN or firewall setting blocking the connection

cases.title: Connected to Wi-Fi but with no internet
cases.meaning: The computer joined the Wi-Fi network, but that network is not giving it a working path to the internet.
causes: The router has no internet from the provider
The computer did not receive a valid IP address
A captive login page that has not been completed

cases.title: USB device not recognized
cases.meaning: Windows detected that something was plugged in but could not identify it or talk to it.
causes: A faulty cable or port
A driver problem
Not enough power from the port or hub

cases.title: The last USB device malfunctioned
patterns: the last usb device you connected to this computer malfunctioned
cases.meaning: Windows tried to use the USB device and it failed to respond properly.
causes: The device or its cable has a fault
A driver problem
A port that is not supplying stable power

cases.title: Printer is offline
cases.meaning: The computer cannot currently reach the printer, even if the printer looks switched on.
causes: The printer lost its Wi-Fi or cable connection
The printer is set to 'Use Printer Offline'
The print queue or spooler is stuck

cases.title: Printer driver is unavailable
cases.meaning: Windows has the printer listed but the software that lets it talk to the printer is missing or damaged.
causes: The driver was removed or damaged after an update
The wrong driver is installed for this printer model

cases.title: Windows cannot connect to the printer
patterns: windows cannot connect to the printer
cases.meaning: Windows could not connect to a shared or network printer. This often appears after a Windows update or when the sharing computer is off.
causes: The computer sharing the printer is off or unreachable
A security change from a recent Windows update
A missing or mismatched driver

cases.title: Print spooler is not running
patterns: print spooler service is not running
cases.meaning: The Windows service that manages print jobs has stopped, so nothing can be sent to any printer.
causes: The spooler service was stopped or crashed
A stuck print job blocking the queue

cases.title: Display driver stopped responding and has recovered
patterns: display driver stopped responding and has recovered
cases.meaning: The graphics driver froze for a moment and Windows restarted it. The screen may flicker or go black for a few seconds when this happens.
causes: An outdated or damaged graphics driver
Heavy graphics load on a computer that is running hot
A graphics settings conflict

cases.title: Monitor says no signal
cases.meaning: The monitor is on but is not receiving a picture from the computer.
causes: A loose or wrong video cable or input selected on the monitor
The computer is asleep or still starting
The graphics output is not sending a signal

cases.title: No audio output device is installed
patterns: no audio output device is installed
audio output device is not plugged in
cases.meaning: Windows cannot find any sound output, so nothing can play through the speakers or headphones.
causes: The audio driver is missing, disabled or damaged
The audio service stopped running
The device is disabled in Windows sound settings

cases.title: Audio service is not running
cases.meaning: The Windows service that handles sound has stopped, so sound stops working until it is restarted.
causes: The Windows Audio service stopped or crashed
A recent driver or Windows update

cases.title: Bluetooth device could not connect
patterns: couldn't connect. try connecting your device again
cases.meaning: Windows could not finish pairing or reconnecting with the Bluetooth device.
causes: The device is not in pairing mode or is out of range
An old pairing that needs to be removed and added again
A Bluetooth driver problem

cases.title: You need to format the disk before you can use it
patterns: you need to format the disk
you need to format the disk in drive
cases.meaning: Windows can see the drive but cannot read its file system. Do not format it if it holds files you need.
causes: The drive was removed without being ejected safely
Corruption in the file system
A new drive that has never been set up

cases.title: The disk is write protected
cases.meaning: Windows will let you read the drive but not save or delete anything on it.
causes: A physical lock switch on the drive or card
A read-only setting on the drive
A drive that has developed a fault

cases.title: Low disk space
patterns: you are running out of disk space
there is not enough space on the disk
cases.meaning: The drive is nearly full, which can stop saving, updating and installing, and can slow the computer down.
causes: Large files, downloads or old updates
Temporary files and the recycle bin

cases.title: File or directory is corrupted and unreadable
patterns: the file or directory is corrupted and unreadable
cases.meaning: Windows could not read part of the drive. Avoid saving anything new to it until it has been checked.
causes: File system errors from an unsafe removal or power loss
A drive that is starting to fail

cases.title: Plugged in, not charging
cases.meaning: The laptop sees the charger but is not charging the battery.
causes: A charger or cable that is not supplying enough power
A battery or power driver problem
A battery that has worn down

cases.title: Consider replacing your battery
cases.meaning: Windows reports that the battery is worn or cannot be read. It may still work, but with much shorter run time.
causes: Normal battery wear over time
A battery that is not detected correctly

cases.title: Computer is low on memory
patterns: your computer is low on memory
cases.meaning: Too many programs are using memory at once, so Windows is struggling to keep everything running.
causes: Too many apps or browser tabs open
A program using far more memory than it should
Not enough memory installed for the work being done

cases.title: Program is not responding
cases.meaning: A program has stopped answering Windows. It is sometimes just busy, and sometimes frozen.
causes: The program is busy with a heavy task
The computer is short on memory or disk speed
A bug or conflict in that program

cases.title: No keyboard detected
patterns: keyboard error or no keyboard present
cases.meaning: The computer could not find a working keyboard at startup.
causes: A loose or unplugged keyboard cable or USB receiver
A keyboard that has no power or a dead battery
A faulty USB port

cases.title: Blue screen: HAL_INITIALIZATION_FAILED
cases.meaning: Windows stopped while it was setting up the basic layer that talks to the hardware, so it could not finish starting. The cause is often a recent change or a problem with a connected device or the drive.
causes: A recent Windows update or driver change
A connected USB device or drive getting in the way
Damaged Windows startup files
A problem with the drive or memory

cases.title: Blue screen: INACCESSIBLE_BOOT_DEVICE
cases.meaning: Windows could not read the drive it needs to start from. It often appears after an update or a change to the drive settings.
causes: A recent Windows update
Damaged Windows startup files
A drive that is not detected or is failing
A changed storage setting

cases.title: Blue screen: UNMOUNTABLE_BOOT_VOLUME
cases.meaning: Windows found the drive but could not open the part of it that holds Windows. The file system on that part may have errors.
causes: File system errors after a sudden shutdown
Damaged Windows startup files
A drive that may be failing

cases.title: Blue screen: CRITICAL_PROCESS_DIED
cases.meaning: A program that Windows cannot run without stopped unexpectedly, so Windows shut itself down to protect your files.
causes: A faulty or recently changed driver
A recent Windows update
Damaged system files
A drive or memory problem

cases.title: Blue screen: SYSTEM_SERVICE_EXCEPTION
cases.meaning: A part of Windows or a driver did something it should not, and Windows stopped to protect itself. It is often linked to a driver or a newly installed app.
causes: A faulty or outdated driver
A newly installed app or update
Damaged system files

cases.title: Blue screen: SYSTEM_THREAD_EXCEPTION_NOT_HANDLED
cases.meaning: A driver or system part hit an error that Windows could not handle. The blue screen may name a file ending in .sys, which points toward the driver involved.
causes: A faulty or outdated driver
A recent Windows update
Damaged system files

cases.title: Blue screen: IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL
cases.meaning: A driver or program tried to use memory in a way it is not allowed to, so Windows stopped. It is most often linked to drivers, and sometimes to memory.
causes: A faulty or outdated driver
A newly installed app or device
A problem with the memory

cases.title: Blue screen: PAGE_FAULT_IN_NONPAGED_AREA
cases.meaning: Windows looked for something in memory that should have been there and could not find it. It is often linked to a driver, an app, or the memory.
causes: A faulty or recently changed driver
A problem with the memory
A drive or file system problem

cases.title: Blue screen: MEMORY_MANAGEMENT
cases.meaning: Windows found a problem in the way memory is being used. It can come from a driver, and sometimes from the memory itself.
causes: A problem with the memory
A faulty or outdated driver
A newly installed app or device

cases.title: Blue screen: KERNEL_SECURITY_CHECK_FAILURE
cases.meaning: Windows noticed that something important in its memory had been changed in the wrong way, and it stopped to protect the computer.
causes: A faulty or outdated driver
A problem with the memory
Damaged system files
A recent Windows update

cases.title: Blue screen: WHEA_UNCORRECTABLE_ERROR
cases.meaning: The computer reported a hardware error that it could not correct. This kind of message can point to a hardware problem, and heat can also play a part.
causes: Too much heat or blocked vents
A problem with the memory, drive or processor
A faulty driver

cases.title: Blue screen: DPC_WATCHDOG_VIOLATION or CLOCK_WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT
cases.meaning: Something kept the computer busy for too long, so Windows stopped. It is often linked to a driver, a storage device, or an old firmware.
causes: A faulty or outdated driver
A problem with the drive
A recent update

cases.title: Blue screen: your PC ran into a problem
patterns: your pc ran into a problem and needs to restart
your device ran into a problem and needs to restart
cases.meaning: Windows has stopped because of an error it could not recover from. The stop code on the same screen tells more about the cause, so write it down.
causes: A faulty or recently changed driver
A recent Windows update
A problem with the memory or drive
Too much heat

cases.title: No bootable device or operating system not found
patterns: reboot and select proper boot device
cases.meaning: The computer could not find Windows on any drive it checked. A USB drive may be getting in the way, or the drive that holds Windows may not be detected.
causes: A USB drive or card left plugged in
The drive that holds Windows is not detected
Damaged startup files
A failing drive

cases.title: BOOTMGR is missing or the boot selection failed
cases.meaning: The first part of Windows that starts the computer could not be found or read. The startup files may be damaged or the drive may not be detected.
causes: Damaged or missing startup files
A USB drive getting in the way
The drive is not detected or may be failing

cases.title: Automatic Repair loop
patterns: automatic repair couldn't repair your pc
cases.meaning: Windows could not start normally, so it is trying to repair itself. If this keeps repeating, Windows needs another way to repair its startup.
causes: Damaged Windows startup files
A recent update or driver change
A forced shutdown while Windows was loading
A drive problem
